```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

BOAT is a Bayesian design for randomized umbrella trials in which the tumor of every enrolled
patient gives patient-derived organoids (PDOs). The PDOs are tested with every treatment open in
the patient's subgroup, so each patient contributes a clinical response to one treatment and PDO
responses to all open treatments. The design

* models patient responses and PDO responses jointly, with a patient random effect shared by
  both,
* clusters the response mean of each treatment across subgroups by reversible jump MCMC, so that
  subgroups with similar effects borrow information,
* drops treatments that are not promising at interim analyses and recommends admissible
  treatments at the end, and
* randomizes each new patient adaptively, favoring the treatment predicted best for this patient
  from the patient's own PDO responses.

This vignette follows a trial from design to conduct to evaluation by simulation. The MCMC runs
below are shortened so that the vignette builds quickly. Use the defaults (10,000 iterations) in
practice.

```{r}
library(BOAT)
```

## 1. Design

The trial below has three subgroups, three experimental treatments and a control. Treatment
$A_2$ is not evaluated in $B_1$ and $A_1$ is not evaluated in $B_3$. Each subgroup enrolls at most
150 patients, with interim analyses after 50% and 75% of them.

```{r}
design <- boat_design(K = 3, J = 3, arms = list(c(0, 1, 3), 0:3, c(0, 2, 3)), N = 150,
                      interim = c(0.5, 0.75), lambda = 0.70, delta_T = 0.05, delta_R = 0.05,
                      mcmc = list(iter = 1000, burn = 500))
design
```

A treatment $A_j$ is admissible in subgroup $B_k$ if it is safe,
$\pi_{T,j} < \pi_{T,0} + \delta_T$, and effective, $\pi_{R,j,k} > \pi_{R,0,k} + \delta_R$. At an
analysis with $n_k$ patients in $B_k$, a treatment is dropped if its posterior probability of
being effective or of being safe is below $c_k = \lambda \sqrt{n_k / N_k}$. At the end the treatments
still open are recommended if both probabilities reach $\lambda$.

```{r}
bounds <- boat_boundary(design)
bounds
```

## 2. Conducting a trial

The data of a trial are two data frames. `pat` has one row per patient with the patient `id`, the
subgroup `k`, the assigned treatment `j` (0 = control), toxicity `YT` and response `YR`. `pdo` has one row per PDO
replicate with the patient `id`, subgroup `k`, the treatment tested `j` and the PDO response
`YO`. Here we simulate one trial from assumed true toxicity and response probabilities and keep
its data. We then go through its analyses as they would be done during the trial.

```{r}
truth <- boat_scenario(pR = rbind(c(0.50, 0.30, NA, 0.70),
                                  c(0.50, 0.70, 0.50, 0.30),
                                  c(0.30,   NA, 0.50, 0.30)),
                       piT = c(0.25, 0.35, 0.20, 0.15))
truth
trial <- boat_simulate_trial(design, truth, seed = 2031, keep_data = TRUE)
pat <- trial$pat
pdo <- trial$pdo
head(pat)
head(pdo)
```

The patients are in the order of enrollment. The function below gives the data available once
each subgroup $B_k$ has enrolled `n[k]` patients or has been stopped. It also gives the number of
patients of each subgroup.

```{r}
data_at <- function(n) {
  keep <- ave(pat$id, pat$k, FUN = seq_along) <= n[pat$k]
  list(pat = pat[keep, ], pdo = pdo[pdo$id %in% pat$id[keep], ], n = tabulate(pat$k[keep], design$K))
}
```

**Before the first interim analysis.** Each patient is randomized equally among the treatments of
the patient's subgroup.

```{r}
boat_randomize(design, k = 1)$prob
```

**Interim analysis 1.** Fit the model to the data of the first 75 patients of each subgroup and
apply the decision rule. `boat_simulate_trial()` runs the MCMC of analysis $l$ with the trial seed
plus $1000 l$, so the seeds below reproduce the decisions of the simulated trial.

```{r}
d1 <- data_at(bounds$n[bounds$analysis == "Interim 1"])
fit1 <- boat_fit(design, d1$pat, d1$pdo, seed = 2031 + 1000)
fit1
dec1 <- boat_decide(design, fit1, n = d1$n)
dec1
```

**Randomization until the next analysis.** Fit the probit models that predict each patient's
response from the patient's PDO responses. Each new patient is then randomized from the patient's
mean PDO response to each open treatment. Below we randomize the next patient of the trial.

```{r}
rar1 <- boat_rar_model(design, d1$pat, d1$pdo, active = dec1$active)
i <- max(d1$pat$id) + 1
pat[pat$id == i, ]
pdo_mean <- with(pdo[pdo$id == i, ], tapply(YO, j, mean))
pdo_mean
boat_randomize(design, k = pat$k[pat$id == i], pdo_mean = pdo_mean, rar = rar1)$prob
```

Without a seed, `boat_rar_model()` continues the random number stream of `boat_fit()` as the
simulation does. Hence, these are the probabilities with which the simulated trial randomized this
patient.

**Interim analysis 2.** Only the treatments still open after interim analysis 1 are evaluated.

```{r}
d2 <- data_at(bounds$n[bounds$analysis == "Interim 2"])
fit2 <- boat_fit(design, d2$pat, d2$pdo, seed = 2031 + 2000)
dec2 <- boat_decide(design, fit2, n = d2$n, active = dec1$active)
dec2
rar2 <- boat_rar_model(design, d2$pat, d2$pdo, active = dec2$active)
```

**Final analysis.** A subgroup stopped at an interim analysis is not reopened, and only the
treatments still open are evaluated. `final = TRUE` gives the recommendations.

```{r}
d3 <- data_at(design$N)
fit3 <- boat_fit(design, d3$pat, d3$pdo, seed = 2031 + 3000)
boat_decide(design, fit3, n = d3$n, active = dec2$active, final = TRUE)
```

These decisions agree with those of the simulated trial.

```{r}
trial
```

## 3. Simulation

`boat_get_oc()` simulates many trials with `boat_simulate_trial()` and summarizes them by
subgroup and treatment. The run below uses 2 trials with short MCMC runs. In practice, use about
1000 trials.

```{r}
fast <- boat_design(arms = list(c(0, 1, 3), 0:3, c(0, 2, 3)), N = 150, lambda = 0.70,
                    mcmc = list(iter = 300, burn = 150), rar_mcmc = list(iter = 200, burn = 100))
oc <- boat_get_oc(fast, truth, nsim = 2)
oc
```

`boat_dgm()` changes the data-generating values, for example the association $\rho$ between the
patient random effect and the PDO responses or the number of PDO replicates $M$.

The tuning parameter $\lambda$ is calibrated so that the largest family-wise error rate over the
subgroups without an admissible treatment is closest to 10%. Under `truth`, subgroup $B_2$ has no
admissible treatment.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cal <- boat_calibrate(design, list(truth), lambda = seq(0.64, 0.76, by = 0.02),
                      nsim = 1000, cores = 8)
cal
```
